name: Judah
overview: Judah was the fourth-born son of Jacob and Leah, belonging to the tribe of Judah. He was a male figure of significant standing in the patriarchal family of Israel. No additional personal notes are recorded beyond these foundational details.
namesAndTitles: The name Judah means 'praised' and is a proper name given to him at birth, as recorded in Genesis 29:35. This name reflects a recognition of praise but was not directly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Judah was one of the sons of Jacob and Leah, making him a brother to Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zebulun, and Dinah. He also had several half-brothers from Jacob's other wives, including Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Joseph, and Benjamin. Additionally, he was the father of Er.
scriptureSignificance: Judah holds a pivotal role in the biblical narrative as the leader among Jacob's sons and the progenitor of the tribe of Judah. His actions, including proposing to sell Joseph rather than kill him, mark significant moments in Israel's history. His personal growth is seen in his willingness to offer himself for his brother Benjamin, demonstrating repentance and responsibility. Importantly, the messianic line, culminating in King David and ultimately Jesus Christ, is traced through Judah, highlighting his lasting spiritual and redemptive significance.
